data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Because, so, although, if, when, before, after
learningPoints: Builds cause and result structures (because, so).
Introduces first conditional for real future situations.
Practises contrast with although and though.
Develops multi-clause sentence control before B1.
ESOL B1 and aligns with IELTS 4.5–5.5 and TOEFL iBT 42–71 score ranges.

words.word: She stayed home because she was sick.
She stayed home so she was sick.
She because was sick stayed home.
It was raining, so we stayed inside.
It was raining because we stayed inside.
So it was raining we stayed inside.
Although it was cold, they went to the beach.
Although it was cold but they went to the beach.
Although was cold they went to the beach.

sections.summary: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb.
sections.explain: Structure: If + present simple, will + base verb.

words.word: If you study, you will pass the exam.
If you will study, you pass the exam.
If you studied, you will pass the exam.

sections.summary: Use 'when' for future time clauses (present form).
sections.explain: After 'when', use present simple for future meaning.

words.word: When I arrive, I will call you.
When I will arrive, I call you.
When I arrived, I will call you.
She washed her hands before she ate dinner.
She washed her hands before she will eat dinner.
Before she washed her hands she ate dinner.

sections.explain: 'After' introduces the later action in sequence.

words.word: He went home after he finished work.
He went home after he will finish work.
After he went home he finished work.

sections.explain: First conditional uses present simple after 'if'.

words.word: If it is sunny, we will travel to the beach.
If it will be sunny, we travel to the beach.
If it was sunny, we will travel to the beach.

sections.summary: Use 'though' to show contrast (similar to although).
sections.explain: 'Though' expresses contrast and does not need 'but'.

words.word: Though he was tired, he continued working.
Though he was tired but he continued working.
Though was tired he continued working.

sections.summary: Correct clause order in first conditional.
sections.explain: Main clause can come first, followed by if-clause.

words.word: We will miss the train if we leave late.
We will miss the train if we will leave late.
We will miss the train if we left late.
